cards.text: Joshua, Israel's leader, and all Israel have been taking city after city in Canaan (Joshua 10). Now Jabin, king of Hazor, hears about these things. So he sends word to Jobab, king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph.

And he keeps going: kings and peoples from the mountains to the foothills, east and west, all the way to the foot of Hermon, a mountain in the north. Friend, Jabin is adding EVERYBODY to the group chat.

cards.question: Jabin's messages go out far and wide. So these kings came out with all their ___.

cards.text: And they don't come light: it's "a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore," with a great number of horses and chariots. I spent years counting dust in a junk drawer, friend, and even I wouldn't try to count THAT.

cards.question: All these kings join forces and set up camp to fight against Israel. Where do they camp?
With that huge army camped against Israel, the LORD speaks to Joshua. What's the first thing He tells him?

answers.text: Do not be afraid of them
Do not go out against them

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Joshua a time: "…by this time tomorrow I will deliver all of them slain before Israel."

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua to hamstring the enemy's horses. What is Joshua to do with their chariots?

cards.text: By the waters of Merom, Joshua and his whole army come upon the kings' armies suddenly and attack.

cards.question: Israel wins the battle at Merom because Israel's army is bigger than the kings' armies.

cards.text: The LORD delivers the kings' armies into Israel's hand, and Israel chases them all the way to Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and east to the Valley of Mizpeh. They strike them down, leaving no survivors.

cards.question: After the battle, Joshua does just what the LORD told him to do with the horses and chariots.

cards.text: At that time, Joshua turns back and heads for Hazor, Jabin's city. Yep, Mr. Group Chat himself.

cards.question: Out of all the cities in the north, why does Joshua turn back for Hazor?

answers.text: It had been the head of all these kingdoms
It had the strongest walls in the whole north
It sat the closest to the camp of Israel

cards.text: Joshua captures Hazor and puts its king to the sword. Everyone in Hazor is devoted to destruction, and Joshua burns Hazor down.

cards.question: Hazor is gone. What does Joshua do with all the other kings and their cities?

answers.text: He lets them keep their land

cards.question: Of all the cities built on their mounds, Hazor is the only one Israel burns.

cards.text: Israel takes the plunder and livestock of these cities for themselves. But the people are put to the sword, with no one who breathed spared.

cards.question: The LORD commanded His servant Moses, Israel's leader before Joshua, and Moses passed it on to Joshua. How much of it does Joshua leave undone?

cards.text: So Joshua takes this entire region, from Mount Halak all the way to the foot of Mount Hermon. He captures all their kings and strikes them down.

cards.question: Joshua's war against all these kings was over in just a few days.
No city made peace with Israel except one. All the others were taken in battle. Who made peace?

cards.text: As for all the others, it was of the LORD to harden their hearts to engage Israel in battle. That way they would be set apart for destruction and receive no mercy, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time, Joshua turns to the Anakim, a people great and tall (Deuteronomy 9:2). He eliminates them from the hill country of Hebron, Debir and Anab, and devotes them to destruction, along with their cities.

cards.question: No Anakim are left in the land of the Israelites. But in three cities, some Anakim survive. Which three?
Joshua took the entire land, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses. Then he gave it to Israel as their ___, by the allotments to their tribes.

cards.text: And after all those battles, the chapter ends with one quiet line: "Then the land had rest from war."
